95	/** @type {Record<number, string|LH.IcuMessage|Record<string, LH.IcuMessage>>} */
96	const FINDING_TO_UI_STRING = {
97	  [Type.MISSING_SEMICOLON]: UIStrings.missingSemicolon,
98	  [Type.UNKNOWN_DIRECTIVE]: str_(UIStrings.unknownDirective),
99	  [Type.INVALID_KEYWORD]: UIStrings.unknownKeyword,
100	  [Type.MISSING_DIRECTIVES]: {
101	    [Directive.BASE_URI]: str_(UIStrings.missingBaseUri),
102	    [Directive.SCRIPT_SRC]: str_(UIStrings.missingScriptSrc),
103	    [Directive.OBJECT_SRC]: str_(UIStrings.missingObjectSrc),
104	  },
105	  [Type.SCRIPT_UNSAFE_INLINE]: str_(UIStrings.unsafeInline),
106	  [Type.PLAIN_WILDCARD]: UIStrings.plainWildcards,
107	  [Type.PLAIN_URL_SCHEMES]: UIStrings.plainUrlScheme,
108	  [Type.NONCE_LENGTH]: str_(UIStrings.nonceLength),
109	  [Type.NONCE_CHARSET]: str_(UIStrings.nonceCharset),
110	  [Type.DEPRECATED_DIRECTIVE]: {
111	    [Directive.REFLECTED_XSS]: str_(UIStrings.deprecatedReflectedXSS),
112	    [Directive.REFERRER]: str_(UIStrings.deprecatedReferrer),
113	    [Directive.DISOWN_OPENER]: str_(UIStrings.deprecatedDisownOpener),
114	  },
115	  [Type.STRICT_DYNAMIC]: str_(UIStrings.strictDynamic),
116	  [Type.UNSAFE_INLINE_FALLBACK]: str_(UIStrings.unsafeInlineFallback),
117	  [Type.ALLOWLIST_FALLBACK]: str_(UIStrings.allowlistFallback),
118	  [Type.REPORTING_DESTINATION_MISSING]: str_(UIStrings.reportingDestinationMissing),
119	  [Type.REPORT_TO_ONLY]: str_(UIStrings.reportToOnly),
120	};
121	
122	/**
123	 * @param {Finding} finding
124	 * @return {LH.IcuMessage|string}
125	 */
126	function getTranslatedDescription(finding) {
127	  let result = FINDING_TO_UI_STRING[finding.type];
128	  if (!result) {
129	    log.warn('CSP Evaluator', `No translation found for description: ${finding.description}`);
130	    return finding.description;
131	  }
132	
133	  // Return if translated result found.
134	  if (isIcuMessage(result)) return result;
135	
136	  // If result was not translated, that means `finding.value` is included in the UI string.
137	  if (typeof result === 'string') return str_(result, {keyword: finding.value || ''});
138	
139	  // Result is a record object, UI string depends on the directive.
140	  result = result[finding.directive];
141	  if (!result) {
142	    log.warn('CSP Evaluator', `No translation found for description: ${finding.description}`);
143	    return finding.description;
144	  }
145	
146	  return result;
147	}
148	
149	/**
150	 * @param {string} rawCsp
151	 */
152	function parseCsp(rawCsp) {
153	  return new CspParser(rawCsp).csp;
154	}
155	
156	/**
157	 * @param {string[]} rawCsps
158	 * @return {{bypasses: Finding[], warnings: Finding[], syntax: Finding[][]}}
159	 */
160	function evaluateRawCspsForXss(rawCsps) {
161	  const parsedCsps = rawCsps.map(parseCsp);
162	  const bypasses = evaluateForFailure(parsedCsps);
163	  const warnings = evaluateForWarnings(parsedCsps);
164	  const syntax = evaluateForSyntaxErrors(parsedCsps);
165	  return {bypasses, warnings, syntax};
166	}
167	
168	module.exports = {
169	  getTranslatedDescription,
170	  evaluateRawCspsForXss,
171	  parseCsp,
172	  UIStrings,
173	};

Verdict, straight through — no more digging.

## Gate table (head `8a16627` vs base `develop`)

| Gate | Base | Head | New violations? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean | clean | None |
| `npm run test` | 26 files / 408 pass | 26 files / 408 pass | None (also: no new test added) |
| `npm run lint` | 20 problems (4 err/16 warn) | identical | None |
| `audit:tokens` | 4 unacknowledged | identical | None |
| CI: Unit tests | — | SUCCESS | Real run |
| CI: Storybook/Playwright/BrowserStack | — | SKIPPED | Expected — shared-path diff, no area match (testing.md's documented skip behavior) |
| Protected File Guard | — | SUCCESS | Blind spot on the Tier 1 file — see findings |

## Findings, ranked by cost to ignore

**1. CONFIRMED — the PR cannot close the Lighthouse finding it's named for.** I traced `csp-xss.js` → `evaluateForFailure` → all six constituent checks in this repo's own installed `csp_evaluator` package, end to end, myself. Every one of them is hardcoded to `DIRECTIVES_CAUSING_XSS = [script-src, object-src, base-uri]` ([security_checks.ts:33-34](node_modules/csp_evaluator/checks/security_checks.ts:33)). `style-src`/`style-src-elem`/`style-src-attr` cannot appear in a `bypasses` finding under any CSP, ever, in this version. Also confirmed: `csp-xss` isn't asserted by name in `lighthouse:recommended` or this repo's own `lighthouserc.js`, so it's not even a blocking CI gate today. The style-src hardening is real, correct, valuable work — it just doesn't do what the ticket and the PR's opening line both say it does. This is a premise problem inherited from the ticket, not a coding mistake.

**2. CONFIRMED (I reproduced it live myself).** `curl` the preview twice, 3s apart: first hit `Miss from cloudfront` with nonce `Ay6/Ins...`, second hit `Hit from cloudfront, age: 3` with the **identical** nonce baked into the same cached HTML. `s-maxage=900` caching means every visitor of a cached homepage/PDP gets the same "per-request" nonce for up to 15 minutes. Still strictly better than the old blanket `unsafe-inline`, but never mentioned anywhere despite the PR otherwise documenting every edge case it hit.

**3. CONFIRMED, should-fix.** `CSP_NONCE_LOCALS_KEY` (`contentSecurityPolicy.ts`) and `AppLocals.cspNonce` (`_app-config/index.tsx`) are two independently-hardcoded spellings of one key, no compiler link. A typo in either silently breaks CSP — no gate catches it.

**4. Should-fix, minor.** No unit test for `getOrCreateNonce`'s memoize-or-generate branch — both independent reviewers agreed this fits testing.md's own bar.

**5. Out of scope for this PR, but real.** `protected-file-guard.yml`'s Tier 1 glob (`overrides/app/ssr.*`) predates the `ssr.js`→`ssr/` split and misses everything under `overrides/app/ssr/**`. CODEOWNERS still gates the file correctly, so merge protection isn't broken — only the automated warning has a blind spot.

**6. Nitpick-adjacent.** Two comment blocks are disproportionately long versus sibling code in the same file; otherwise the unusually dense commenting throughout is justified — I verified nearly every factual claim in it against real package source and it all held up.

## Scope verdict

Solid, well-verified engineering, correctly and honestly scoped away from `script-src` (verified that's structurally unfixable from this repo). But it does not deliver what it claims to deliver against the named Lighthouse audit. That's the one call that changes what "done" means here.

---
name: project-sfcc856-csp-review
description: SFCC-856 CSP hardening (PR #79) approved despite not closing the named Lighthouse csp-xss audit; script-src is structurally locked by the SDK
metadata:
  type: project
---

PR #79 (TimLavelleACC, branch `fix/SFCC-856-csp-hardening-v2`, superseding stale PR #76) implemented nonce-based CSP for `style-src` in `overrides/app/ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts` + `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx`. Reviewed 2026-09-01 via zimmerMANNReview; approved by Marcel ("nothing but nitpicks") over my recommendation to request changes first. See [[feedback_review_verdict_severity]] for the verdict-calibration pattern this confirmed a second time.

**Why this matters going forward — two structural facts, not just this PR's bug list:**

1. **`csp-xss` (the Lighthouse audit SFCC-856 is named for) cannot be affected by any `style-src` change, in this exact installed toolchain.** Traced `node_modules/lighthouse/lighthouse-core/audits/csp-xss.js` → `csp-evaluator.js` → `csp_evaluator`'s `evaluateForFailure` → all six constituent checks are hardcoded to `DIRECTIVES_CAUSING_XSS = [script-src, object-src, base-uri]` (`csp_evaluator/checks/security_checks.ts:33-34`). `style-src`/`style-src-elem`/`style-src-attr` cannot appear in a `bypasses` finding. Also confirmed `csp-xss` isn't asserted by name in `lighthouse:recommended` or this repo's own `lighthouserc.js`, so it isn't a CI-blocking gate today either — SFCC-856 must be tracked via a manual/external Lighthouse run.
2. **`script-src`'s `'unsafe-eval'` is structurally un-removable from this repo.** `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime`'s `defaultPwaKitSecurityHeaders` (applied in the absolutely-frozen `overrides/app/ssr.js`) monkey-patches `res.setHeader` so that *any* later CSP header this app sets — including helmet's — gets forcibly union-merged with the SDK's own required `script-src` values (`'unsafe-eval'`, `runtimeAdmin`, `*.site.com`). No app-level change can opt out short of forking the SDK.

**How to apply:** if a future ticket revisits SFCC-856 or any `script-src`/`csp-xss` work, start from these two facts rather than re-deriving them — the real fix (if one exists at all) is a `script-src` nonce/`strict-dynamic` strategy that survives the SDK's forced merge, not more `style-src` work. Also worth revisiting: PR #79's own nonce is diluted by `s-maxage=900` CDN caching on homepage/PDP (same nonce replayed to every visitor of a cache entry for up to 15 min, confirmed live) — still strictly better than the prior blanket `unsafe-inline`, but not a true per-request secret; no code fix exists within `overrides/` for this either (would need edge-compute nonce rewriting on cache HIT, or dropping HTML caching, both bigger calls).
